application.description: A recruitment tracker for a staffing agency. Recruiters post open roles, add candidates with contact details and a CV, move candidates through interview stages, and schedule interviews. Hiring managers review candidates that reach offer stage.
application.name: Recruitment Tracker

businessRules.expression: on create Role: status = 'open' AND closedAt IS NULL
businessRules.name: New roles start open
businessRules.statement: A role that a recruiter posts is open from the moment it is saved, and only an explicit close action can take it out of the open-roles list.

businessRules.expression: length(btrim(Role.title)) > 0 AND Role.description IS NOT NULL AND Role.clientOrDepartment IS NOT NULL
businessRules.name: A role must say what the job is and who it is for
businessRules.statement: A role cannot be saved without a real title, a description and the client or department it is being recruited for.

businessRules.expression: Role.openingsCount IS NULL OR Role.openingsCount > 0
businessRules.name: A role advertises at least one opening
businessRules.statement: If a recruiter states how many positions a role has, that number must be at least one.

businessRules.expression: on create Application: Role.status = 'open'
businessRules.name: A closed role takes no new candidates
businessRules.statement: Once a role is closed nobody can be attached to it; the recruiter must reopen the role first.

businessRules.expression: Role.status = 'closed' does not change Application.status or Application.currentStage
businessRules.name: Closing a role keeps its candidates visible
businessRules.statement: Closing a role removes it from the default open-roles list but every candidate already attached to it stays visible on the role and on the candidate's history.
businessRules.syncNote: Whether closing a role should force its still-active applications to a terminal state is unstated; this rule deliberately leaves them active, matching the REQ-003 acceptance criterion and FLOW-003.

businessRules.expression: (Role.status = 'closed') = (Role.closedAt IS NOT NULL)
businessRules.name: A closed role records when it was closed
businessRules.statement: A role is either open with no closing date or closed with the date it was closed - never one without the other.

businessRules.expression: UNIQUE (lower(Candidate.email))
businessRules.name: One candidate record per email address
businessRules.statement: The agency keeps a single record per person: an email address already in the directory cannot be used to create a second candidate, regardless of capitalisation.

businessRules.expression: exists Candidate where lower(email) = lower(input.email) -> return recoverable conflict naming that candidate id
businessRules.name: A duplicate email offers the existing person, not an error
businessRules.statement: When a recruiter enters an email that already exists, they are shown the existing candidate and offered a link to it rather than a constraint failure.

businessRules.expression: not exists Candidate where lower(email) = lower(input.email) AND id <> subject.id
businessRules.name: Editing a candidate does not flag their own email as a duplicate
businessRules.statement: When a candidate record is saved after editing, the duplicate-email check ignores the record being edited.

businessRules.expression: length(btrim(Candidate.fullName)) > 0 AND Candidate.email matches address format; Candidate.phone may be null
businessRules.name: A candidate needs a name and a valid email; a phone number is optional
businessRules.statement: A candidate cannot be saved without a real name and a well-formed email address, but may be saved with no phone number.

businessRules.expression: UNIQUE (CandidateDocument.candidateId) WHERE kind = 'cv' AND isCurrent; the clearing of the prior flag commits in the same transaction as the insert
businessRules.name: A candidate has at most one current CV
businessRules.statement: Uploading a new CV makes it the candidate's current CV and the previous one immediately stops being current, so the record never shows two current CVs.

businessRules.expression: on replace: insert new CandidateDocument row with a fresh storageKey; prior row retained with isCurrent = false
businessRules.name: Replaced CVs are kept, not overwritten
businessRules.statement: An earlier CV version stays retrievable after it is replaced; a replacement never deletes or reuses the stored file of the version it supersedes.
businessRules.syncNote: Versioning is inferred on ENTITY-004: REQ-005 only requires that a second upload replaces the current CV. If simple overwrite is confirmed, this rule is dropped.

businessRules.expression: CandidateDocument.fileSizeBytes > 0 AND contentType in accepted document types AND fileSizeBytes <= configured ceiling, evaluated before the blob write
businessRules.name: A file is checked before it is stored
businessRules.statement: An uploaded document's type and size are validated on the server before any file is written to storage, and an empty file is always rejected.

businessRules.expression: CandidateDocument.storageKey, bucket paths and signed URLs are never present in any API response
businessRules.name: CVs are served only through an authorised download
businessRules.statement: A CV is delivered by an endpoint that checks the requester's permission and streams the file; the storage location is never given out to a browser.

businessRules.expression: UNIQUE (Application.candidateId, Application.roleId)
businessRules.name: A candidate is attached to a role only once
businessRules.statement: The same candidate cannot be attached twice to the same role; the second attempt is explained as an existing application rather than failing.

businessRules.expression: on create Application: currentStage = 'applied' AND status = 'active' AND stageEnteredAt = now AND one ApplicationStageEvent with eventType='created', fromStage IS NULL, toStage='applied'
businessRules.name: A new application starts at the first stage
businessRules.statement: Attaching a candidate to a role creates an active application at the first pipeline stage, together with the opening entry of its stage history.
businessRules.syncNote: The stage vocabulary is inferred on ENTITY-005; only 'offer' is named by the requirements. Confirm the agency's real stage list.

businessRules.expression: Application.currentStage and Application.status are per (candidateId, roleId) pair and are never derived across a candidate's other applications
businessRules.name: Each of a candidate's applications tracks its own stage
businessRules.statement: A candidate can be considered for several roles at once and their progress in one role never affects their stage in another.

businessRules.expression: Application.status = 'active' AND Role.status = 'open' AND targetStage <> Application.currentStage
businessRules.name: Only an active application on an open role can be moved
businessRules.statement: A recruiter can advance or move back only an application that is still active and belongs to a role that is still open.

businessRules.expression: any write to Application.currentStage or Application.status appends exactly one ApplicationStageEvent with changedByUserId = session.userId and changedAt = now, atomically
businessRules.name: Every stage change is written to history
businessRules.statement: Every move, rejection and reopening records the stage moved from, the stage moved to, the time and the acting user, in the same transaction as the change itself.

businessRules.expression: no role holds update or delete on ApplicationStageEvent; no client-facing write endpoint exists
businessRules.name: Stage history cannot be edited or erased
businessRules.statement: A stage history entry, once written, is never changed or deleted by anyone, so the pipeline can always be explained after the fact.

businessRules.expression: on stage change: Application.stageEnteredAt = now
businessRules.name: Time in stage is measured from the last move
businessRules.statement: Each time an application changes stage its stage-entry date is restamped, so the pipeline and the offer review always show how long the candidate has been where they are.

businessRules.expression: Application.status = 'rejected' excludes the row from the pipeline view; the row is never deleted and stays listed on the candidate record
businessRules.name: A rejected application leaves the pipeline but is never deleted
businessRules.statement: Rejecting an application takes it out of the role's active pipeline while the record stays retrievable on the candidate's history with its reason and author.

businessRules.expression: (Application.status = 'rejected') = (Application.rejectedAt IS NOT NULL)
businessRules.name: A rejected application records when it was rejected
businessRules.statement: An application is either not rejected and carries no rejection date, or rejected and carries the date it was rejected.

businessRules.expression: (Application.currentStage = 'offer' AND Application.status = 'active') OR exists OfferDecision where applicationId = Application.id AND decidedByUserId = session.userId
businessRules.name: A hiring manager sees only offer-stage candidates
businessRules.statement: A hiring manager can see an application only while it is active at offer stage, or where they themselves have already recorded a decision on it; every role, candidate, CV, interview and stage entry they can read is reached through such an application.

businessRules.expression: Candidate.notes is excluded from every payload served to a hiring_manager
businessRules.name: Internal recruiter notes stay with the recruiter
businessRules.statement: A hiring manager reviewing an offer-stage candidate sees contact details, the CV and interview outcomes, but not the recruiter's internal notes on the person.
businessRules.syncNote: Inferred, not stated - carried over from the PERM-010 syncNote. Confirm with the product owner whether hiring managers should read recruiter notes.

businessRules.expression: UNIQUE (OfferDecision.applicationId) WHERE supersededAt IS NULL
businessRules.name: An application holds one live offer decision at a time
businessRules.statement: Once an approve or decline has been recorded on an application, no further decision can be recorded until a recruiter reopens it.

businessRules.expression: write to OfferDecision requires session.userRole = 'hiring_manager'
businessRules.name: Only a hiring manager records an offer decision
businessRules.statement: A recruiter can never approve or decline an offer; the decide affordance is absent from every recruiter surface, not merely disabled.

businessRules.expression: no update or delete on OfferDecision; on Application reopen: OfferDecision.supersededAt = now where supersededAt IS NULL, and supersededAt >= decidedAt
businessRules.name: A decision is corrected by reopening, never by editing
businessRules.statement: A recorded offer decision is never edited or deleted; a recruiter reopening the application supersedes it, keeps it on the record as history, and frees the application for a fresh decision.

businessRules.expression: OfferDecision rows for an application, live and superseded, are readable by role 'recruiter' on PAGE-011
businessRules.name: The recruiter sees the decision and who made it
businessRules.statement: An offer decision, its author, its timestamp and any comment are visible to the recruiter on the application, including decisions that have since been superseded.

businessRules.expression: on create or reschedule Interview: scheduledAt > now
businessRules.name: An interview is booked in the future
businessRules.statement: An interview cannot be scheduled or rescheduled to a date and time that has already passed.

businessRules.expression: Interview.durationMinutes > 0 AND Interview.durationMinutes <= 480
businessRules.name: An interview lasts between one minute and eight hours
businessRules.statement: An interview must have a positive length that fits inside a working day.

businessRules.expression: Application exists AND Application.status = 'active' AND Interview.interviewerName IS NOT NULL AND Interview.locationOrLink IS NOT NULL
businessRules.name: An interview names an active application, an interviewer and a place to meet
businessRules.statement: An interview can only be booked against an existing active application and must record who is conducting it and either the address or the meeting link.

businessRules.expression: Interview.status = 'scheduled' AND Interview.scheduledAt >= now, ordered by scheduledAt ascending
businessRules.name: The upcoming agenda shows only live future bookings
businessRules.statement: The upcoming-interviews list shows scheduled interviews soonest first and leaves out anything cancelled or already in the past.

businessRules.expression: (Interview.status = 'cancelled') = (Interview.cancelledAt IS NOT NULL); the row is never deleted; cancelling requires status = 'scheduled' and an explicit confirmation
businessRules.name: A cancelled interview stays on the application
businessRules.statement: Cancelling an interview drops it out of upcoming lists and records when it was cancelled, but the booking remains on the application record and is never deleted.

businessRules.expression: update to Interview.scheduledAt, durationMinutes, mode, locationOrLink or interviewer requires status = 'scheduled'; outcomeNotes remain writable
businessRules.name: A cancelled or completed interview can no longer be rescheduled
businessRules.statement: Once an interview is cancelled or marked completed, only its outcome notes may still be changed.

businessRules.expression: postedByUserId, createdByUserId, uploadedByUserId, changedByUserId, scheduledByUserId, decidedByUserId = session.userId; ignored if present in the request body
businessRules.name: The system records who acted, not who the request claims acted
businessRules.statement: The user recorded against a posted role, a new candidate, an upload, a stage move, a booking or a decision is always taken from the signed-in session and any value supplied by the client is ignored.

businessRules.expression: read scope for role 'recruiter' is unfiltered by postedByUserId, createdByUserId, scheduledByUserId or changedByUserId
businessRules.name: Recruiters share the whole agency's book of work
businessRules.statement: Any recruiter can see and work every role, candidate, application and interview in the agency; the recorded author of a record is attribution for the audit trail, not a visibility filter.

businessRules.expression: sign_in requires User exists AND password matches AND User.isActive = true; all failures return one identical message; an existing session for a deactivated user is rejected on its next request
businessRules.name: A deactivated user cannot sign in and is told nothing extra
businessRules.statement: Sign-in fails for an unknown email, a wrong password and a deactivated account alike, with the same message, so the form cannot be used to discover who has an account.

businessRules.expression: User.passwordHash excluded from every API response and log line
businessRules.name: Stored credentials never leave the server
businessRules.statement: A user's stored password is never returned by any part of the application and never appears in a log.

businessRules.expression: every route except /sign-in resolves session.userId or redirects to /sign-in with an empty payload
businessRules.name: Nobody sees agency data before signing in
businessRules.statement: A visitor who is not signed in is sent to the sign-in page from any other route and is returned no role, candidate, application or interview data.

businessRules.expression: recruiter -> /overview, hiring_manager -> /offer-review; hiring_manager on /overview, /roles, /candidates, /applications or /interviews returns permission_denied
businessRules.name: Each role lands on the surface it owns
businessRules.statement: After signing in, a recruiter lands on the workspace overview and a hiring manager on the offer review queue; a hiring manager reaching a recruiter surface is refused with a way back to their own queue.

businessRules.expression: all route guards and entity writes evaluate session.userRole server-side on every request
businessRules.name: Permission is enforced on the server, not in the interface
businessRules.statement: Hiding a navigation entry or disabling a button is presentation only; every route and every write re-checks the signed-in user's role on the server.

businessRules.expression: Candidate.email, phone, location, linkedinUrl, notes excluded from logs and from payloads that do not render them
businessRules.name: Candidate contact details stay out of logs and list payloads
businessRules.statement: A candidate's email, phone, location, profile link and notes are treated as personal data: they are not written to logs and are returned only where a surface actually displays them.

businessRules.expression: time_in_stage(n) = ApplicationStageEvent[n+1].changedAt - ApplicationStageEvent[n].changedAt; current stage measured from Application.stageEnteredAt to now
businessRules.name: Time spent at each earlier stage is read from history
businessRules.statement: How long a candidate spent at each earlier stage is calculated from consecutive stage-history entries, never from a figure a user can type in.

businessRules.expression: on reject or reopen: ApplicationStageEvent.eventType in ('rejected','reopened') AND fromStage = toStage = Application.currentStage at the moment of the event; Application.currentStage is not changed
businessRules.name: Rejection and reopening are recorded without moving the candidate between stages
businessRules.statement: Rejecting or reopening an application records the event against the stage the candidate was actually sitting at, so the history shows where they fell out or came back in rather than inventing a move.
businessRules.syncNote: Currently unenforceable: the ENTITY-006 CHECK (from_stage IS NULL OR from_stage <> to_stage) forbids fromStage = toStage on a non-created event, and CHECK ((event_type='created')=(from_stage IS NULL)) forbids a null fromStage here. FLOW-009 and FLOW-010 are blocked on the same conflict. A change request against data asks for terminal and non-moving event types to be exempted from the inequality check.

businessRules.expression: transition Interview.status 'scheduled' -> 'completed' requires scheduledAt <= now
businessRules.name: An interview is only marked completed after it was due to happen
businessRules.statement: A recruiter can only mark an interview completed once its scheduled time has passed; a future booking is either scheduled or cancelled.
businessRules.syncNote: Matches the FLOW-014 guard (status = 'scheduled' AND scheduledAt <= now). No requirement states it explicitly; it is the only reading that keeps the agenda and the outcome record coherent.

businessRules.expression: any write to Interview leaves Application.currentStage, Application.status and Application.stageEnteredAt unchanged and appends no ApplicationStageEvent
businessRules.name: Booking or completing an interview never moves the application by itself
businessRules.statement: Scheduling, completing or cancelling an interview leaves the application exactly where it is; only an explicit recruiter action advances, moves back, rejects or reopens it.
businessRules.syncNote: Stated so the stage vocabulary containing an 'interview' stage is not mistaken for automation: no requirement or workflow couples interview lifecycle to stage movement.

businessRules.expression: on create OfferDecision: Application.currentStage, Application.status and Application.stageEnteredAt unchanged; no ApplicationStageEvent appended
businessRules.name: Recording an offer decision does not itself move the application
businessRules.statement: An approve or decline is a recorded outcome only; the application stays active at offer stage until a recruiter marks the hire or rejects it, so the recruiter remains the only person who moves the pipeline.
businessRules.syncNote: Matches FLOW-015 and TEST-040, which assert no stage or status change on decide. Confirm with the product owner whether an approval should automatically drive the application to 'hired'; today it does not.

businessRules.expression: write to OfferDecision re-evaluates Application.currentStage = 'offer' AND Application.status = 'active' inside the writing transaction; otherwise permission_denied
businessRules.name: A decision is refused once the application has left offer stage
businessRules.statement: If an application stops being an active offer-stage application between the moment the hiring manager loads the queue and the moment they decide, the decision is refused and explained rather than written late.
businessRules.syncNote: Closes the race PERM-017 describes for the read path but which no rule covered for the write path.

businessRules.expression: on reopen: Application.status = 'active' AND rejectedAt = NULL AND stageEnteredAt = now; prior ApplicationStageEvent rows unchanged
businessRules.name: Reopening returns an application to active and clears its rejection
businessRules.statement: Reopening an application makes it active again and removes its rejection date, while the rejection itself stays visible in the stage history.
businessRules.syncNote: Required by the ENTITY-005 CHECK pairing status='rejected' with rejectedAt; RULE-023 stated the pairing but nothing stated that reopening must clear the date.

businessRules.expression: Application.status <> 'hired' OR Application.currentStage = 'hired'
businessRules.name: A hired application sits at the hired stage
businessRules.statement: An application can only be marked hired when it has reached the final stage of the pipeline, so a hire is never recorded against a candidate still shown mid-process.
businessRules.syncNote: Mirrors the existing ENTITY-005 CHECK, which had no business rule behind it. The 'hired' stage and status are part of the inferred stage vocabulary flagged on ENTITY-005.

businessRules.expression: Application.status = 'withdrawn' excludes the row from the pipeline view and from active counts; the row is never deleted and stays listed on the candidate record
businessRules.name: A withdrawn application leaves the pipeline like a rejected one
businessRules.statement: When a candidate withdraws, the application drops out of the role's active pipeline but stays on the candidate's history with its stage timeline intact.
businessRules.syncNote: Inferred: 'withdrawn' exists in the ENTITY-005 status enum but no requirement, page action or workflow ever sets it. Either confirm a withdraw action (and it needs its own workflow and stage event type) or drop the enum value.

businessRules.expression: hiring_manager read of CandidateDocument requires kind = 'cv' AND isCurrent = true AND the owning candidate is on an Application readable under application.read_offer_stage
businessRules.name: A hiring manager retrieves only the candidate's current CV
businessRules.statement: At offer review a hiring manager can open the CV the candidate is currently represented by, and nothing else the agency holds on file - no superseded versions and no other documents.
businessRules.syncNote: States the scope PERM-014 already carries; RULE-014 covered how a CV is served but not which documents a hiring manager may reach.

businessRules.expression: no delete endpoint or delete affordance exists for Role, Candidate, CandidateDocument, Application, ApplicationStageEvent, Interview or OfferDecision; retirement is expressed through status, isCurrent or supersededAt
businessRules.name: Nothing in the tracker is deleted
businessRules.statement: Roles are closed, applications are rejected, interviews are cancelled, CVs are superseded and decisions are superseded - no record is ever removed, so any hiring outcome can still be explained afterwards.
businessRules.syncNote: Consistent with every page action, permission and workflow in the Blueprint, none of which deletes. The cascade onDelete rules on data.relationships therefore only describe what an out-of-band administrative delete would do; no application path reaches them. If a data-retention or GDPR erasure obligation is confirmed, this rule needs an explicit exception and its own requirement.

businessRules.expression: queue = Application where currentStage = 'offer' AND status = 'active' AND NOT EXISTS OfferDecision where applicationId = Application.id AND supersededAt IS NULL, ordered by stageEnteredAt ascending
businessRules.name: The offer review queue puts the longest-waiting candidate first
businessRules.statement: The offer review queue is ordered by how long each candidate has been waiting at offer stage, longest first, and an application that already carries a live decision drops out of the queue.
businessRules.syncNote: Ordering and the decided-item exclusion were asserted in PAGE-015, WIDGET-018 and TEST-037 but never stated as a rule. The exclusion needs a join the widget dataSource shape cannot express, so it is applied by the backing endpoint.

businessRules.expression: count(Application where candidateId = Candidate.id AND status = 'active'); non-active applications remain listed on the candidate record
businessRules.name: A candidate's role count reflects live applications only
businessRules.statement: The number of roles a candidate is applied to counts only the applications still in play; rejected, withdrawn and hired applications stay on the record but are not counted as current activity.
businessRules.syncNote: REQ-017 asks for 'the number of roles they are currently applied to' without defining 'currently'; TEST-052 already assumes active-only. Confirm whether a hired application should still be counted.

If the engine expects a different predicate dialect these strings need a single global rename, not a structural change.; Tabs was deliberately avoided for related collections because its childContract requires children to match props.tabs, and the tab labels are only known per page after the repeat expands; Accordion + AccordionPanel gives the same grouping with a contract a repeat can satisfy.; record_workspace is used in this Blueprint for both pure create/edit forms (/roles/new, /candidates/new) and read-heavy workspaces (/applications/[id], /offer-review/[id]), so the template carries both a form region and a summary/history rail, each gated so the unused half collapses.; configuration is the closest enum fit for /sign-in and the non-visual / redirect, so the template keeps loading and error as first-class siblings of the form rather than assuming a form is always present.; No AppShell, SideNav or top bar appears in any template; page chrome is treated as layout-owned.

If the planner does not supply groupByField, cardBadgeField, cardHref or rowHref, those props degrade to unresolved bindings rather than breaking structure.; Application chrome (AppShell, SideNav, breadcrumbs, top bar) is excluded from every template as layout-owned; templates describe the page body only.; configuration is used here for sign-in and for the non-visual entry redirect, so its form card is intentionally generic and its loading state is a normal sibling; the redirect page will simply render the headline plus LoadingState because it contributes no form fields.; record_workspace covers both create forms (/roles/new, /candidates/new, /interviews/new) and dense workspaces (/applications/[id], /candidates/[id], /offer-review/[id]); the accordion of related collections is empty for create forms and the right rail collapses to summary-only, which is why the split degrades at lg rather than md.; Tabs was avoided in favour of Accordion for related collections because Tabs requires a tabs[] prop that cannot be generated from a repeat while honouring its one-child-per-panel contract.

value.rationale: One scannable working list per page: a headline band carrying the page's own name and purpose plus its promoted create/navigate CTAs, an optional metric strip so a list page can state the size of its working set, a filter/search bar, then the record table driven by the page's own columns. Every page-specific part is a placeholder or a repeat, so Roles, Candidate Directory and Upcoming Interviews all fit without the template naming any of them. The widgets strip and the related-collections tail are repeats, so a page with none of them pays nothing.

An answer-first landing surface: headline band with the page's purpose and its promoted jump-off CTAs, then every widget the planner hands over as a metric tile in a four-up grid (staggered so the strip reads as one rhythm rather than ten separate boxes), then a two-up band pairing a recent-activity feed with the primary entity's own table, then one card per related collection. All quantities come from repeats, so a dashboard with three widgets and one with ten both compose correctly.

A decision queue reads top-down: what state is the queue in (widgets as tiles), how do I narrow it (filter bar), what is waiting (one selectable table over the page's own columns, oldest-first ordering supplied by the page's data), and what supporting collections exist. Row-level open/decide affordances belong to the table's own row actions, which the planner derives from the page's actions, so the template promotes only the page's primary actions into the headline band and never hard-codes an approve or decline control that some readers of the same page are not permitted to see.

Built only from $page.name and $page.purpose plus repeats, because one page in this group (the entry redirect) has no primary entity at all and must not touch $entity.* or $formFields as a bare value. A narrow centred container holds a single card: the page's own fields as a repeat inside a Form, and the page's actions as submit buttons. A page with no fields and one action (the redirect) renders as a purpose statement with one continue affordance; a page with fields (sign-in) renders as a credential card. No entity name, no table, no chrome.

The board is the page, so everything above it stays to one line: headline band with the page's purpose, then a single toolbar row pairing filter/search with the page's own actions as light buttons (stage moves and rejection are card-level and are carried by the board's own move affordances). Cards are titled and described from the entity's own title and subtitle fields, with the entity's summary fields as card detail, so the same template serves any board over any entity. Related collections tail the board for context.

A persistent list beside a working record. SplitView's contract is honoured exactly: two children, master then detail. Master is search plus the entity's own column set; detail leads with the record's actions, then its summary fields as a description list, then any optional metric tiles, then one card per related collection using that collection's own columns — which is how a role detail shows its attached candidates and applications without the template knowing what a role is. Selection is deep-linked through syncKey so a detail pane is shareable.

value.rationale: One template that has to serve both create/edit forms and read-and-work record pages, so nothing is conditional on which it is: a 2:1 split whose main column carries the record's editable fields inside a Form (empty repeat on a read page — the card then simply reads as the record's own panels) followed by one card per related collection, and whose aside carries the record's summary fields, an action list built from the page's own actions, and a read-only history timeline. Promoted actions render as the form's submit row so create and edit pages get their primary CTA in the place the eye already is; the remaining actions sit in the aside so a nine-action workspace does not turn its header into a wall of buttons. The history timeline is presentational only, which keeps audit trails read-only by construction.

changeHistory.smithInterpretation: Seven templates authored, one per distinct pattern in use: approval_inbox, configuration, dashboard, entity_list, kanban, master_detail, record_workspace. No pattern was invented and none was split.; The configuration template is built only from $page.name, $page.purpose and repeats, because Entry Redirect (/) has no primary entity; no $entity.*, $titleField, $columns or $formFields appears as a bare value there.; I treat `primaryActions` as the promoted subset the planner wants rendered as a page CTA / form submit, and `actions` as the remaining page-level affordances. To avoid the same button appearing twice, no template repeats over both in the same visual region, and only kanban and record_workspace use `actions` at all (as a toolbar and an aside action list respectively).; `$item.value` on an action item is assumed to be the resolvable target (route or workflow) and is passed to Button.onClick, which the catalog types as `any`, rather than to `navigate`/`workflow` which are typed as strings and would break for the other kind of target.; Runtime data bindings written as {{items}}, {{record}}, {{selected}}, {{activity}} and {{history}} are assumed to be the planner's standard page-scope bindings for the primary collection, the loaded record, the selected master row, the activity feed and the audit history; they pass through untouched per the placeholder rules.; The `Text` component is documented with no props, so no template relies on it; all prose is carried by Section title/subtitle and Heading-free structural containers.; Per-row affordances (open, reject, download) are left to Table/Kanban row actions derived from each page's actions rather than being hard-coded into the templates, which also keeps role-gated affordances (e.g. a recruiter reading the offer queue with no decide control) resolvable at plan time.; No AppShell, SideNav or top bar appears in any template; those belong to the layout.

value.rationale: Landing-surface shape: a headline band naming the page and its purpose, a metric band that expands to one tile per widget (10 on Workspace Overview, none on a leaner dashboard), then a 2:1 split where the wide side carries the primary entity's recent records and the narrow rail carries every page action as a jump-off list. No action buttons in the headline, so the rail is the single home for actions and nothing is rendered twice.

Collection shape shared by Roles, Candidate Directory and Upcoming Interviews: headline with the page's primary CTAs, an optional single-row metric strip (each of these pages carries exactly one count widget, and the repeat emits nothing if a future list page carries none), then the collection itself in a titled card. Table is configured searchable so per-page search/filter actions have a home without the template inventing a search endpoint it cannot know.

Two-pane record shape: headline with the record's primary actions, then SplitView honouring its exact master/detail child contract. Master is the browsable collection of the primary entity; detail is the selected record's summary followed by one card per related collection (attached candidates, applications), which is how Role Detail earns its second pane. Detail panes degrade to the SplitView empty text when nothing is selected.

value.rationale: One shape for both halves of this group: the pure create/edit forms (Post a Role, Add Candidate, Schedule Interview, the two edit pages) and the read-heavy workspaces (Candidate Record, Application Workspace, Interview Detail, Offer Review). Every page here has a primary entity, so the headline carries the full action set as a wrapping cluster (Application Workspace needs nine of them and none may be hidden), the wide column carries the declarative Form over the page's own form fields followed by one card per related collection (CV history, applications, interviews, stage history), and the narrow rail carries the record summary so identifying facts stay visible while editing. A create form simply has no related collections and an empty summary, and a read-only page simply has no form fields.

Board shape: headline with the board-level actions (attach candidate, toggle rejected), then a single full-width card hosting Kanban over the primary entity, with card title and description drawn from the entity's own title and subtitle fields. Per-card stage moves are the Kanban component's own affordance rather than template structure, so no action rail competes with the board.

Queue shape: headline with the queue's own controls, a metric strip for the waiting counts the page carries as widgets, then the queue itself as a titled table over the primary entity ordered by the page's own query. Related collections (already-decided items) append as further cards, so a decided view needs no second template. Row-level decide affordances belong to the row actions the planner supplies, keeping the template free of role-specific buttons that must not render for recruiters.

Built for both pages in the group, one of which (Entry Redirect, /) has no primary entity at all, so nothing here reads $entity.*, $titleField, $columns or $formFields as a bare value. Structure is a narrow single-column body: a headline stating what the page is for, then one card whose contents are a focus-managed form whose inputs come from a repeat over the page's form fields (two on Sign In, none on the redirect route) and a trailing action cluster. On the redirect route the repeat emits nothing and the card degrades to the page's single action, which is the correct non-visual fallback rather than a blank screen.

changeHistory.smithInterpretation: Collection components are bound to the page's primary records through the runtime binding {{records}}, which passes through untouched; related collections are bound through $item.value inside the relatedCollections repeat.; $columns and $item.columns are column descriptor arrays acceptable to Table.columns, and $formFields is a field descriptor array acceptable to Form.fields (declarative mode), mirroring how $columns feeds Table.; $summaryFields is an array of label/value entries acceptable to DescriptionList.items.; A repeated action item exposes $item.value as the workflow/handler identifier, so Button.workflow carries it; navigation-style actions are expected to be resolved by the workflow layer rather than Button.navigate, since the template cannot know a route.; primaryActions is a small headline subset of actions rather than the same list, so no template renders both except record_workspace, which deliberately renders the full actions set only (nine on Application Workspace, all of which must remain reachable).; Prop strings are kept to exact-match placeholders (e.g. title: "$entity.plural") rather than interpolated prose, so no page can leak a literal "$entity" into visible copy if substitution is exact-match only.; Application chrome (AppShell/SideNav) and per-page state components (loading/empty/error/permission-denied) are supplied by the layout and the page's own bound components (CMP-002/003/034), not by these templates.

decisions.decision: Interview Scheduling (MODULE-004) as specified in modules
decisions.reason: pages[] bound. PAGE-013 is normally reached with an application pre-selected from a pipeline card, the application workspace or the candidate record, and also stands alone from the navigation shortcut with an application picker.

decisions.decision: Offer Review (MODULE-005) as specified in modules
decisions.reason: pages[] bound. PAGE-015 is the hiring manager's initial route and is also readable by recruiters (PERM-036) with no decide affordance; PAGE-016 is hiring-manager only (PERM-037).

decisions.decision: Access Control (MODULE-006) as specified in modules
decisions.reason: pages[] bound. Neither page appears in navigation.tree by design: /sign-in renders outside the app shell and / is a non-visual redirect whose targets mirror navigation.initialRoute. Navigation entries now carry roles[] restrictions using ROLE-001 and ROLE-002.

decisions.decision: Roles (PAGE-002) as specified in pages
decisions.reason: Recruiter-only (PERM-032); hiring managers receive permission_denied here. Empty state: 'No open roles yet' with a Post a Role action; filtered-empty (no closed roles) is distinct copy from never-created-empty. DataTable (CMP-033) collapses to stacked cards on mobile.

decisions.decision: Post a Role (PAGE-003) as specified in pages
decisions.reason: Recruiter-only. No empty state (a create form is never empty). Error state covers inline field validation (missing title/description/client) and save failure with the entered values preserved. Shares RoleForm (CMP-006) with /roles/[id]/edit.

decisions.decision: Role Detail (PAGE-004) as specified in pages
decisions.reason: Recruiter-only. Empty state = role exists but no candidates attached yet, offering Attach Candidate. Error state must distinguish an unknown/deleted role id (not-found variant of CMP-003) from a load failure (retry). Closed roles render read-mostly: attached candidates stay visible (RULE-005) but Attach Candidate is disabled. Attaching a candidate is AttachCandidateDialog (CMP-017) on this page, not a separate route.

decisions.decision: Edit Role (PAGE-005) as specified in pages
decisions.reason: Recruiter-only. Error state covers not-found role id, inline validation, and concurrent-update/save failure. status and closedAt are never written from this form; Close Role goes through CloseRoleDialog (CMP-007) and FLOW-003.

decisions.decision: Role Pipeline (PAGE-006) as specified in pages
decisions.reason: Recruiter-only; a hiring manager reaching this route gets permission_denied (PERM-032). Columns follow Application.currentStage (applied, screening, interview, offer, hired) - flagged as inferred on ENTITY-005, so the column set must be re-derived if the stage vocabulary changes. Moves are applied optimistically and rolled back visibly on refusal (FLOW-008). On mobile the board degrades to one stage list at a time with a stage selector.

decisions.decision: Candidate Directory (PAGE-007) as specified in pages
decisions.reason: Recruiter-only (PERM-033); hiring managers reach candidate data only through /offer-review/[id]. Two distinct empty states are required by REQ-017: an untouched directory ('No candidates yet - Add Candidate') and a search with no matches ('No candidate matches "x" - Add them'). Search is debounced and server-side, backed by the lower(full_name) and lower(email) prefix indexes.

decisions.decision: Add Candidate (PAGE-008) as specified in pages
decisions.reason: Recruiter-only. Error state covers inline email-format validation (mirrors the DB CHECK on ENTITY-003) and the unique-email conflict, which CandidateForm (CMP-010) must render as a recoverable warning linking to the existing candidate (RULE-008), not a raw constraint error. Phone is optional by REQ-004.

decisions.decision: Candidate Record (PAGE-009) as specified in pages
decisions.reason: Recruiter-only. ApplicationsPanel (CMP-037) and InterviewsPanel (CMP-038) are now bound, resolving the earlier note that they existed only as in-flight proposals. Panel-level empty states are mandatory: no CV yet renders an upload prompt inside CvPanel (CMP-012) rather than an error (REQ-005), no applications yet offers Attach to Role inside CMP-037, and no interviews yet reads as normal inside CMP-038. Error state distinguishes unknown candidate id from load failure, and an upload failure must not lose the rest of the page.

decisions.decision: Edit Candidate (PAGE-010) as specified in pages
decisions.reason: Recruiter-only. Shares CandidateForm (CMP-010) with /candidates/new; the duplicate-email check must exclude the record being edited (RULE-009). Error state covers not-found, validation and save conflict.

decisions.decision: Application Workspace (PAGE-011) as specified in pages
decisions.reason: Recruiter-only. InterviewsPanel (CMP-038) and OfferDecisionPanel (CMP-039) are now bound, resolving the earlier note that they existed only as in-flight proposals. Stage history is read-only in the UI - no edit or delete affordance (RULE-020) - and no approve or decline affordance appears anywhere on this page (RULE-027); CMP-039 carries none by construction. Empty state applies to the interviews panel (no interviews yet) and the decision panel (not at offer stage / no decision recorded). Reopening supersedes the live OfferDecision, which must still be shown as history (RULE-029).

decisions.decision: Upcoming Interviews (PAGE-012) as specified in pages
decisions.reason: Recruiter-only (PERM-035). Empty state: 'No interviews scheduled' with a Schedule Interview action - a common and legitimate state, not an error. Default view is the day-grouped UpcomingInterviewsList (CMP-035); the past/cancelled view reuses DataTable (CMP-033). Backed by the partial index on scheduled_at WHERE status='scheduled'. Mobile is first-class because recruiters check the agenda on the move; a calendar/scheduler pattern was rejected as heavier than REQ-013 asks for.

decisions.decision: Schedule Interview (PAGE-013) as specified in pages
decisions.reason: Recruiter-only. Application context arrives as a query parameter; without it InterviewForm (CMP-021) must offer an application picker (combobox) rather than failing. Error state covers past-date rejection (RULE-030), duration outside 1-480 minutes (RULE-031), and save failure with input preserved.

decisions.decision: Offer Review Queue (PAGE-015) as specified in pages
decisions.reason: users[] lists ROLE-002 first because this is the hiring manager's initial route; ROLE-001 is included because PERM-036 lets recruiters read the queue, but no decide affordance may be rendered for them and the row action for a recruiter must route to /applications/[id] rather than /offer-review/[id], which PERM-037 denies them. Backed by the partial index on (current_stage, stage_entered_at). Empty state ('Nothing awaiting your decision') is the normal resting state and must read as reassurance, not failure.

decisions.reason: Currently unenforceable: the ENTITY-006 CHECK (from_stage IS NULL OR from_stage <> to_stage) forbids fromStage = toStage on a non-created event, and CHECK ((event_type='created')=(from_stage IS NULL)) forbids a null fromStage here. FLOW-009 and FLOW-010 are blocked on the same conflict. A change request against data asks for terminal and non-moving event types to be exempted from the inequality check.

decisions.decision: Booking or completing an interview never moves the application by itself (RULE-047) as specified in businessRules
decisions.reason: Stated so the stage vocabulary containing an 'interview' stage is not mistaken for automation: no requirement or workflow couples interview lifecycle to stage movement.

decisions.decision: Recording an offer decision does not itself move the application (RULE-048) as specified in businessRules
decisions.reason: Matches FLOW-015 and TEST-040, which assert no stage or status change on decide. Confirm with the product owner whether an approval should automatically drive the application to 'hired'; today it does not.

decisions.decision: A decision is refused once the application has left offer stage (RULE-049) as specified in businessRules
decisions.reason: Closes the race PERM-017 describes for the read path but which no rule covered for the write path.

decisions.decision: Reopening returns an application to active and clears its rejection (RULE-050) as specified in businessRules
decisions.reason: Required by the ENTITY-005 CHECK pairing status='rejected' with rejectedAt; RULE-023 stated the pairing but nothing stated that reopening must clear the date.

decisions.decision: A hired application sits at the hired stage (RULE-051) as specified in businessRules
decisions.reason: Mirrors the existing ENTITY-005 CHECK, which had no business rule behind it. The 'hired' stage and status are part of the inferred stage vocabulary flagged on ENTITY-005.

decisions.decision: A hiring manager retrieves only the candidate's current CV (RULE-053) as specified in businessRules
decisions.reason: States the scope PERM-014 already carries; RULE-014 covered how a CV is served but not which documents a hiring manager may reach.

decisions.decision: Nothing in the tracker is deleted (RULE-054) as specified in businessRules
decisions.reason: Consistent with every page action, permission and workflow in the Blueprint, none of which deletes. The cascade onDelete rules on data.relationships therefore only describe what an out-of-band administrative delete would do; no application path reaches them. If a data-retention or GDPR erasure obligation is confirmed, this rule needs an explicit exception and its own requirement.

decisions.decision: The offer review queue puts the longest-waiting candidate first (RULE-055) as specified in businessRules
decisions.reason: Ordering and the decided-item exclusion were asserted in PAGE-015, WIDGET-018 and TEST-037 but never stated as a rule. The exclusion needs a join the widget dataSource shape cannot express, so it is applied by the backing endpoint.

decisions.decision: A candidate's role count reflects live applications only (RULE-056) as specified in businessRules
decisions.reason: REQ-017 asks for 'the number of roles they are currently applied to' without defining 'currently'; TEST-052 already assumes active-only. Confirm whether a hired application should still be counted.

integrations.name: Email + Password Session Auth
integrations.syncNote: Matches security.authentication = 'email_password' and ENTITY-001.passwordHash: credentials are verified locally against the users table, no external identity provider is involved. Covers PERM-001 (session.sign_in), the non-enumerating failure message shared by bad credentials and User.isActive = false, the lastLoginAt stamp on success, and the signed session cookie that every protected route in security.protectedRoutes is resolved from. AUTH_SECRET signs/encrypts the session cookie; AUTH_PASSWORD_HASH_ROUNDS is the argon2/bcrypt cost factor and is configuration rather than a true secret - drop it from secretRefs if the generator only accepts secrets. No self-service password reset, invite or email-verification flow exists in the Blueprint, so this integration ships no outbound mail: user rows are provisioned by seed/admin means that no requirement yet describes. If an external IdP (Google Workspace, Entra, agency SSO) is later chosen, this artifact's provider changes and ENTITY-001.passwordHash must be replaced with a provider subject identifier - see the ENTITY-001 syncNote.

integrations.name: Candidate Document Storage
integrations.syncNote: Object store holding the CV and other CandidateDocument blobs (ENTITY-004). Only the opaque storageKey is persisted in Postgres; the bytes live here. provider is deliberately blank because no requirement or prior section names a storage vendor - any S3-compatible bucket (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2) or Vercel Blob satisfies the contract, and the secretRefs above assume the S3-compatible shape; a Vercel Blob choice collapses them to a single BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN. Behaviour this integration must honour, already fixed by earlier sections: (1) uploads are validated server-side for content type and size before the blob is written (PERM-012, security.ownershipRules), and ENTITY-004 CHECK (file_size_bytes > 0) rejects empty files; (2) replacement is versioned, not overwrite - a new key is written and isCurrent is cleared on the prior row in the same transaction (REQ-005), so keys must be unique per upload and never reused; (3) reads are brokered - PERM-013/PERM-014 and security.ownershipRules forbid returning storageKey, a bucket path or a signed URL to any client, so the download endpoint streams the object after authorising the actor. That rules out browser-direct uploads/downloads against the bucket unless the security section is amended. Retention: no requirement asks for deletion, and superseded CV versions stay retrievable, so no lifecycle expiry rule is set.

integrations.name: Transactional Email
integrations.syncNote: Inferred and unconfirmed - propose dropping unless the product owner confirms it. No requirement in the Blueprint asks for any outbound message: ENTITY-007.interviewerEmail and ENTITY-003.email are recorded as contact details only, REQ-011/REQ-012 say nothing about notifying an interviewer or candidate when an interview is booked, moved or cancelled, REQ-014/REQ-015 say nothing about alerting a hiring manager that an application reached offer stage or a recruiter that a decision was recorded, and REQ-016 defines no password-reset or invite flow. It is registered here so the dependency is visible rather than discovered late, because an ATS that stores an interviewer address and never writes to it is usually a gap. Nothing is wired to it yet: no page action, permission or widget depends on it, so removing this artifact costs nothing today. If confirmed, it needs new requirements (who is notified, on which events, and whether cancellation withdraws a prior invite) plus a delivery-failure story for the recruiter, since a silently dropped interview invitation is worse than no invitation. provider is blank pending that decision; the secretRefs shape fits Resend/Postmark/SendGrid-style API senders and would change for SMTP relay.

See a clear reason when sign-in fails

Jump to the next upcoming interviews

Jump to roles or the candidate directory to start work

See how many active applications each role carries
Filter to closed roles or search by title/client

Start posting a new role

Optionally set location, employment type and number of openings
Save and land on the new role

See all attached candidates with their current stage and time in stage
Attach an existing candidate to this role
Open an application to move it or schedule an interview

Error state must distinguish an unknown/deleted role id (not-found variant of CMP-003) from a load failure (retry). Closed roles render read-mostly: attached candidates stay visible (RULE-005) but Attach Candidate is disabled. Move an application back a stage with a note

Columns follow Application.currentStage (applied, screening, interview, offer, hired) - flagged as inferred on ENTITY-005, so the column set must be re-derived if the stage vocabulary changes. Open a candidate record
Add a candidate that genuinely does not exist yet

See interviews scheduled for this candidate

roles.syncNote: Name matches the ENTITY-001.userRole enum value and the navigation.initialRoute key. No create, update or delete on any entity other than OfferDecision.

ownershipRules: Every request outside /sign-in resolves the acting user from the session; an unauthenticated request to any other route redirects to /sign-in and returns no role, candidate or application data (REQ-016).
A User with isActive = false cannot sign in and any existing session is rejected on the next request; sign-in failure and inactive-account failure return the same non-enumerating message.

Authorisation is by role, not by record ownership: recruiters see every role, candidate, application and interview in the agency. postedByUserId, createdByUserId, uploadedByUserId, scheduledByUserId and changedByUserId are attribution for the audit trail and must never be used as an access filter.

All actor columns (postedByUserId, createdByUserId, uploadedByUserId, scheduledByUserId, changedByUserId, decidedByUserId) are set server-side from the session and are ignored if present in a request body.

A hiring manager may read an Application only while currentStage = offer AND status = active, or where they have themselves recorded a decision on it. Every other hiring-manager read - role, candidate, CV, interview, stage event - is granted only via an application that passes this test.
Hiring managers have no access to the /roles, /candidates, /applications or /interviews route trees, to the candidate directory search, or to Candidate.notes.
ApplicationStageEvent is append-only: no role holds update or delete, and rows are written only inside the transaction that performs the stage transition (REQ-018).

OfferDecision may be written only by a hiring manager, only when no row for that application has supersededAt IS NULL. Decisions are never updated or deleted; a recruiter reopening the application supersedes the live row and unlocks a fresh decision (REQ-015).
Recruiters may not create, update or delete an OfferDecision under any circumstance; the decide affordance is absent from every recruiter surface, not merely disabled.

CandidateDocument blobs are served only through an authorisation-checked download endpoint that resolves storageKey server-side; storage keys, signed URLs and direct bucket paths are never returned to a client.
Uploads are validated server-side for content type and size before the blob is stored, and a replacement CV clears isCurrent on the previous row in the same transaction (REQ-005).
Sensitive candidate fields (email, phone, location, linkedinUrl, notes) and User.passwordHash are excluded from list payloads and logs; passwordHash is never returned by any endpoint.
Route guards are enforced server-side on every request. Hiding a navigation entry or disabling a button is presentation only and is never the sole control.

tests.name: A newly posted role is saved with status open and no closedAt
tests.syncNote: Asserts RULE-001: create ignores any client-supplied status or closedAt and forces open with closedAt null, and postedByUserId comes from the session (RULE-036).

tests.name: A role cannot be saved without a real title, a description and a client or department
tests.syncNote: Covers the REQ-001 criterion that a submission without a title is rejected with a validation message and no role row is written; whitespace-only title is rejected too.

tests.name: Openings count is either absent or greater than zero
tests.syncNote: Direct insert of openings_count = 0 and -1 must violate the CHECK; NULL must be accepted.

tests.name: POST /api/roles creates a role for a recruiter and refuses a hiring manager
tests.syncNote: Recruiter receives the created role; hiring_manager receives permission_denied; unauthenticated receives a redirect or 401 with no body data.

tests.name: The roles list returns open roles newest first and closed roles only when filtered
tests.syncNote: Seeds two open and one closed role; default response excludes the closed role and orders by createdAt descending.

tests.name: Opening a role shows its details plus every attached candidate and each current stage
tests.syncNote: Second REQ-002 acceptance criterion. Also asserts the not-found variant for an unknown role id rather than a blank error.

tests.name: Roles list renders title, client or department and status, with distinct empty states
tests.syncNote: Never-created empty state offers Post a Role; filtered-to-nothing reads as no matches, not as a failure.

tests.name: Closing a role removes it from the open list while its candidates stay visible
tests.syncNote: FLOW-003 end to end: confirmation required, status closed with closedAt stamped, attached applications keep their status and currentStage (RULE-005), reopen clears both.

tests.name: A role is open with no closing date or closed with one, never mismatched
tests.syncNote: Both mismatch directions must violate the CHECK.

tests.name: Editing a role saves details and cannot set status or closedAt
tests.syncNote: status, closedAt and postedByUserId supplied in the body are ignored by the generic update path (PERM-006, RULE-036).

tests.name: A candidate needs a name and a well-formed email but no phone number
tests.syncNote: Covers all three REQ-004 criteria: valid save appears in the directory, malformed email rejected with a validation message, phone omitted saves cleanly.

tests.name: One candidate record per email address regardless of capitalisation
tests.syncNote: Inserting the same address with different casing must violate the unique index on lower(email).

tests.name: Saving an edited candidate does not flag their own email as a duplicate
tests.syncNote: Saving with the unchanged email succeeds; changing to another candidate email returns the recoverable conflict.

tests.name: Uploading a CV stores the file and shows its name on the candidate record
tests.syncNote: FLOW-006 happy path against a stubbed storage adapter; asserts the document row, isCurrent true, uploadedByUserId from the session, and the file name rendered in the CV panel.

tests.name: A second CV upload becomes current and the previous one stops being current
tests.syncNote: Covers RULE-011 and RULE-012: exactly one current CV after replacement, the superseded row retained with a distinct storageKey, and the flag clearing committed in the same transaction.

tests.name: An empty, oversized or wrong-type file is refused before anything is stored
tests.syncNote: Asserts the storage adapter is never called on a rejected upload and no CandidateDocument row is written (RULE-013).

tests.name: A candidate with no CV shows an upload prompt rather than an error
tests.syncNote: Third REQ-005 criterion, and an upload failure must not clear the rest of the page.

tests.name: A CV is streamed by an authorised endpoint and its storage location is never returned
tests.syncNote: No response body or header on any candidate or document payload contains storageKey, a bucket path or a signed URL (RULE-014); an unauthenticated request is refused.

tests.name: A hiring manager can retrieve the current CV of an offer-stage candidate only
tests.syncNote: Current CV of an offer-stage active application is downloadable; a superseded version, another document kind, and any candidate below offer stage are refused (PERM-014).

tests.name: Attaching a candidate to an open role creates an active application at the first stage with its opening history entry
tests.syncNote: FLOW-007: currentStage applied, status active, stageEnteredAt stamped, and exactly one stage event with eventType created, fromStage null, toStage applied, written in the same transaction.

tests.name: Attaching the same candidate to the same role twice is refused with an explanation
tests.syncNote: Third REQ-007 criterion. The second attempt names the existing application and links to it instead of surfacing the unique-constraint failure (RULE-015).

tests.name: A closed role accepts no new candidates until it is reopened
tests.syncNote: RULE-004: attach is refused while closed and succeeds after reopening; the Attach affordance is disabled on the closed role.

tests.name: A candidate on several roles keeps a separate stage for each application
tests.syncNote: Second REQ-007 criterion: advancing one application leaves the other candidate-role pair untouched (RULE-017).

tests.name: Advancing or moving back an application restamps its stage entry and appends one history entry
tests.syncNote: FLOW-008: exactly one ApplicationStageEvent per move naming the session user; a rejected application or a closed role blocks the move and the optimistic card rolls back visibly (RULE-018).

tests.name: Moving an application to offer stage makes it appear in the hiring manager queue
tests.syncNote: Second REQ-008 criterion: invisible to the hiring manager before the move, listed oldest-waiting first after it.

tests.name: Current stage is displayed wherever an application is listed
tests.syncNote: Third REQ-008 criterion; the badge also renders the lifecycle status so a rejected row is legible on the candidate record.

tests.name: Rejecting an application removes it from the pipeline but keeps it on the candidate history
tests.syncNote: Both REQ-009 criteria plus the reason and author on the timeline. Blocked on the FLOW-009 conflict: the ENTITY-006 CHECK forbids fromStage = toStage on a non-created event, so a rejection that does not move stage cannot currently be written; the test asserts the retained row and will need the resolved shape of the rejected event.

tests.name: A rejected application carries a rejection date and a non-rejected one does not
tests.syncNote: Both mismatch directions violate the CHECK; reopening must clear rejectedAt.

tests.name: The role pipeline groups every non-rejected application by stage with candidate name and stage entry date
tests.syncNote: Both REQ-010 criteria. Rejected and withdrawn applications are absent from the board by default; the empty board offers Attach Candidate.

tests.name: Scheduling an interview against an application records time, interviewer and place and lists it on the candidate and the role
tests.syncNote: FLOW-011: status scheduled, scheduledByUserId from the session, booking visible on the candidate record, the application and the agenda. Booking against a non-active application is refused (RULE-032).

tests.name: An interview cannot be scheduled or rescheduled into the past
tests.syncNote: Second REQ-011 criterion: a past date/time is rejected with a validation message on both create and reschedule, with input preserved.

tests.name: Interview length must be between one minute and eight hours
tests.syncNote: 0, negative and 481 minutes violate the CHECK; 1 and 480 are accepted.

tests.name: Rescheduling a scheduled interview updates its time or interviewer without creating a second booking
tests.syncNote: First REQ-012 criterion; status, cancelledAt, applicationId and scheduledByUserId supplied in the body are ignored (FLOW-012).

tests.name: Cancelling an interview drops it from upcoming lists but keeps it on the application
tests.syncNote: Second REQ-012 criterion: explicit confirmation, status cancelled with cancelledAt stamped, row never deleted and still listed on the application (RULE-034).

tests.name: A cancelled or completed interview accepts only outcome notes
tests.syncNote: RULE-035: time, duration, mode, location and interviewer writes are refused; outcomeNotes still save.

tests.name: The upcoming interviews list is soonest first and excludes past and cancelled bookings
tests.syncNote: Both REQ-013 criteria: each row carries date/time, candidate, role, interviewer and mode across every role; a past scheduled booking and a cancelled future booking are both absent.

tests.name: A hiring manager sees only offer-stage active applications in the queue
tests.syncNote: First and third REQ-014 criteria plus PERM-017: applications below offer stage are absent, an application that leaves offer stage between load and open returns permission_denied, and an application the manager already decided stays readable.

tests.name: Offer review shows contact details, the CV, the interviews held and time spent at each earlier stage
tests.syncNote: Second REQ-014 criterion and the fourth REQ-018 criterion. Also covers the no-CV and no-interviews states and the absence of any edit affordance.

tests.name: Recruiter notes are absent from every payload served to a hiring manager
tests.syncNote: Asserts RULE-025, which the Blueprint itself flags as inferred. If the product owner confirms hiring managers may read notes, this test is inverted or dropped.

tests.name: A hiring manager approves or declines an offer-stage application with an optional comment
tests.syncNote: FLOW-015 for both outcomes: decidedByUserId and decidedAt set server-side, supersededAt null, and no stage or status change on the application.

tests.name: The decision, its author, its time and any comment are visible to the recruiter
tests.syncNote: Second REQ-015 criterion, including superseded decisions kept as history after a reopen (RULE-029), and the not-at-offer-stage and no-decision panel states.

tests.name: A decided application cannot be decided again until a recruiter reopens it
tests.syncNote: Third REQ-015 criterion end to end: the second decide attempt is refused, a concurrent attempt fails closed on the partial unique index, and reopening stamps supersededAt, appends a reopened history entry and unlocks a fresh decision.

tests.name: A recruiter can never record an offer decision and is offered no decide affordance
tests.syncNote: Third REQ-016 criterion: the decide endpoint refuses a recruiter session, and no approve or decline control is rendered on any recruiter surface, absent rather than disabled (RULE-027).

tests.name: An unauthenticated visitor is sent to sign-in and receives no agency data
tests.syncNote: First REQ-016 criterion, exercised over every entry in security.protectedRoutes: redirect to /sign-in with an empty payload, no role, candidate, application or interview data.

tests.name: Unknown email, wrong password and deactivated account all fail with the same message
tests.syncNote: RULE-038: identical message and status for all three cases, lastLoginAt stamped only on success, and an existing session for a deactivated user rejected on its next request.

tests.name: A recruiter lands on the overview and a hiring manager on the offer review queue
tests.syncNote: FLOW-016 routing mirrors navigation.initialRoute; an unrecognised userRole falls back to /sign-in with a message rather than a blank screen.

tests.name: A hiring manager reaching a recruiter surface is refused with a way back to their own queue
tests.syncNote: Second REQ-016 criterion: the whole /roles, /candidates, /applications and /interviews trees plus /overview return permission_denied, and the create-role, add-candidate and stage-move writes are refused server-side even when called directly (RULE-041, RULE-042).

tests.name: A stored password never appears in an API response or a log line
tests.syncNote: RULE-039 and RULE-043: passwordHash absent from every payload, and candidate email, phone, location, profile link and notes absent from captured log output.

tests.name: A partial name or email filters the candidate directory to matching people
tests.syncNote: Second REQ-017 criterion; matching is case-insensitive on both name and email and the search runs server-side.

tests.name: An untouched directory and a search with no matches read differently and both offer Add Candidate
tests.syncNote: Third REQ-017 criterion; neither state may render as an error.

tests.name: An email already on file warns the recruiter and offers the existing candidate
tests.syncNote: Fourth REQ-017 criterion: a recoverable conflict naming the existing candidate id with a link, never a raw constraint error, and no second row created (RULE-008).

tests.name: The candidate directory shows each person's name, email and the number of roles they are currently applied to
tests.syncNote: First REQ-017 criterion. The count covers active applications only; rejected and withdrawn ones are excluded from it while remaining on the candidate record.

tests.name: Stage history cannot be edited or deleted by anyone
tests.syncNote: Third REQ-018 criterion: no client-facing create, update or delete endpoint exists for stage events under either role, and the timeline renders with no edit or delete affordance (RULE-020).

tests.name: Stage history lists every transition chronologically with from-stage, to-stage, time and acting user
tests.syncNote: First and second REQ-018 criteria: after create, advance, move back, reject and reopen the timeline holds one entry per action in order, each naming the session user who performed it (RULE-019, RULE-036).

tests.name: Time spent at each earlier stage is computed from consecutive history entries
tests.syncNote: RULE-044: earlier stages measured between adjacent changedAt values, the current stage from stageEnteredAt to now, and no user-entered figure is accepted.

tests.name: The application boots, serves the sign-in page and answers a health check
tests.syncNote: Cheapest possible failure signal before the suites above run.

tests.name: The project type-checks, builds and applies every migration to an empty database
tests.syncNote: Also asserts every constraint and index in data.constraints exists after migration, since several tests above depend on them being enforced at the database level.

tests.name: Actor columns are taken from the session and ignored when supplied by the client
tests.syncNote: RULE-036 across every write path: posting a role, adding a candidate, uploading a CV, attaching a candidate, moving a stage, booking an interview and recording a decision each store the signed-in user, and a forged postedByUserId, createdByUserId, uploadedByUserId, changedByUserId, scheduledByUserId or decidedByUserId in the request body is discarded rather than honoured or rejected.

tests.name: A recruiter sees roles, candidates, applications and interviews created by other recruiters
tests.syncNote: RULE-037 and security.ownershipRules: seeded by recruiter A, read by recruiter B. Lists, searches and detail routes must return the same rows for both sessions, proving attribution columns are never used as an access filter.

tests.name: Stage history entries satisfy the created/from-stage pairing and the movement check
tests.syncNote: Direct inserts: eventType 'created' with a non-null fromStage violates the pairing CHECK; a non-created event with a null fromStage violates it too; fromStage = toStage on a non-created event violates the movement CHECK. That last case is exactly the shape FLOW-009 and FLOW-010 need for 'rejected' and 'reopened' events, so this test currently pins a constraint the Blueprint's own workflows cannot satisfy - it must be rewritten to the exempted shape once the data change request lands.

tests.name: A decision cannot be superseded before it was recorded and only one live decision exists per application
tests.syncNote: supersededAt earlier than decidedAt violates the CHECK; equal timestamps are accepted. A second row with supersededAt IS NULL for the same application violates the partial unique index, while a second row inserted after the first is superseded is accepted.

tests.name: A hired application must sit at the hired stage
tests.syncNote: RULE-051, which had no test behind it: status 'hired' with currentStage 'interview' or 'offer' violates the CHECK; status 'hired' at stage 'hired' is accepted; a non-hired status at stage 'hired' is also accepted. Depends on the inferred stage vocabulary flagged on ENTITY-005.

tests.name: An interview can only be marked completed once its scheduled time has passed
tests.syncNote: RULE-046 and the FLOW-014 guard: completing a future booking is refused, completing a past scheduled booking succeeds, and a cancelled booking can never become completed. No requirement states this explicitly, so the test inherits RULE-046's confidence.

tests.name: Recording an interview outcome saves the notes and surfaces them at offer review
tests.syncNote: FLOW-014 end to end, which no existing test exercised: a past scheduled interview is marked completed, outcomeNotes are saved, notes remain editable on a completed or cancelled booking, and the notes are then readable by a hiring manager on an offer-stage application through PERM-026 while staying invisible below offer stage.

tests.name: Booking, completing or cancelling an interview never moves the application by itself
tests.syncNote: RULE-047: after each interview write, Application.currentStage, status and stageEnteredAt are byte-identical to before and the stage-history row count is unchanged. Guards against the 'interview' stage in the enum being mistaken for automation.

tests.name: A decision is refused if the application leaves offer stage before it is submitted
tests.syncNote: RULE-049 covers the write path that TEST-037 only covered for reads: the hiring manager loads the review page, a recruiter then moves the application back a stage or rejects it, and the submitted decision is refused with an explanation and no OfferDecision row. Re-evaluation happens inside the writing transaction, so a concurrent move must not allow a late write.

tests.name: The offer review queue is longest-waiting first and hides applications already decided
tests.syncNote: RULE-055: three offer-stage applications with different stageEnteredAt values come back ascending by that column, an application holding a live OfferDecision is absent from the default queue and present when show-decided is toggled, and an application whose decision has been superseded by a reopen returns to the queue. The exclusion is asserted at the endpoint because the WIDGET-018 dataSource shape cannot express the join.

tests.name: Nothing in the tracker can be deleted through any endpoint or affordance
tests.syncNote: RULE-054: a DELETE against every entity collection and item route is refused for both roles (method not allowed or permission_denied, never a successful removal), and no delete control is rendered on any recruiter or hiring-manager surface. Retirement is only reachable through status, isCurrent and supersededAt.

tests.name: Navigation shows only the entries the signed-in role owns and offers sign-out
tests.syncNote: CMP-031 against navigation.tree: a recruiter session renders Overview, Roles, Candidates, Interviews and Offer Review; a hiring-manager session renders Offer Review only. Paired with TEST-047, which proves the hiding is presentation and the server refuses the routes anyway (RULE-042).

tests.name: Dashboard aggregates count the right rows and return zero rather than failing on an empty database
tests.syncNote: The three metrics endpoints (roles, applications, interviews) had no test. Open-role count excludes closed roles, pipeline count excludes rejected, withdrawn and hired applications, awaiting-decision count is offer-stage active only, and interview count excludes cancelled and past bookings. On an empty database each returns zero so the tiles render a zero state, and the recent-stage-moves feed comes back newest first because the endpoint applies descending changedAt before truncating to the limit.

tests.name: Schedule Interview offers an application picker when no application is pre-selected
tests.syncNote: CMP-021 on PAGE-013: reached from the navigation shortcut with no query parameter the form renders a picker over active applications rather than erroring; reached with a valid application id it renders that context read-only. Past-date and out-of-range-duration errors appear inline with the entered values preserved.

tests.name: A replaced CV stays retrievable by a recruiter and keeps its own stored file
tests.syncNote: RULE-012 retrievability, which TEST-015 asserted only at row level: after a replacement the earlier document downloads successfully for a recruiter through the brokered endpoint, its storageKey differs from the new one and was not overwritten, and the CV panel lists it as an earlier version. Inherits the ENTITY-004 syncNote - if simple overwrite is confirmed, this test is dropped.

Drop it with the enum value if the product owner confirms no withdraw action, or extend it once a withdraw workflow and stage event type exist.

workflows.name: Record Offer Decision
workflows.purpose: Brings the hiring manager into the process at offer stage and captures the outcome in the tracker rather than in email (REQ-014, REQ-015). One live decision per application: a second attempt is refused until a recruiter reopens, and the recorded decision with its author and timestamp becomes visible to the recruiter on the application workspace.

steps.name: Hiring manager opens an offer-stage candidate

config.expression: application.currentStage = 'offer' AND application.status = 'active' AND NOT EXISTS offer_decision WHERE applicationId = application.id AND supersededAt IS NULL

steps.name: Check the application is still awaiting a decision

cases: A live decision exists: the form is replaced by the decision, its author and timestamp and stays disabled until a recruiter reopens.
The application left offer stage between queue load and open: permission_denied per PERM-017.

steps.name: Show the recorded decision or deny access

config.note: Everything on this surface is read-only; Candidate.notes is withheld (RULE-025).

steps.name: Review candidate, CV, interviews and time in stage
Approve or decline with an optional comment

config.guard: Partial unique index on (application_id) WHERE supersededAt IS NULL makes a concurrent second decision fail closed.

steps.name: Write the offer decision

config.mechanism: Read-only panel on /applications/[id] (PAGE-011) via PERM-030 and API-052 on next load; no write and no outbound message because INT-003 is unconfirmed.

steps.name: Decision becomes visible to the recruiter

Decision recorded and locked

workflows.name: Sign In and Role Landing
workflows.purpose: The single entry process (REQ-016): verifies credentials locally, refuses inactive accounts with the same non-enumerating message as bad credentials, stamps lastLoginAt, and routes the user to the surface their role owns so nobody needs to know a URL.
